entries.text: A small company in a shared, indifferent sky.

Everything under this sky is shared. The air, the ducts, the hulls that creak like something asleep, and every credit anyone earns, which goes into the Common Ledger and comes back in portions. The Plan is generous. It is also five cycles long, and then another five.

Four markets: Military, Luxury, Minerals, Biotech. Each has rivals, and the Plan counts every share each cycle. Hold over half of one market and the count stops being a rumour.

So you have a small company, one ship's worth of cash, three planets and two goods. Buy where it is cheap. Sell where it is not. Serving the common good is encouraged. Profit, officially, is a typing error.

What it costs the sky, the sky does not say.

entries.text: A garrison has a war to feed

The Admiralty wills Ashgate's high-ring garrison to keep fighting, and Quartermaster Hanno Sulo wills the invoices to match. He bought your first cargo. {bot1} once sent him painted ballast marked as shells. He offers a standing contract with a deposit, or cash by the lot.
Get: Military volume up a little for a while. Cost: {cash_out} credits as the deposit to the garrison. Rivals: {bot1}'s Military growth falls a little.

Sulo signed with a seal and kept {bot} as a second source, on probation. Orders now come on a schedule and the deposit cost you credits, so Military volume rises for a while. {bot}'s Military growth falls a little. Each crate is read a litany on the dock, and one rattled.

entries.text: A new admiral orders new sensors

New Admiral Gabe Nuer took the high ring, and the next day came an order: fit his tracking sensors or pay a heavy port fee. Only his cousin's firm sells them, through {bot1}'s berths, in blessed crates. {bot3} had its own sensors ready. Someone wants the whole market.
Get: {cash_in} credits now. Cost: Ship upkeep rises clearly for a while. Rivals: {bot1}'s Military strength falls sharply.

You sent the order, the price list and the cousin's name to the Bureau. It paid an informant's fee and froze half the refit berths for audit. Your ships stand in queues, so Ship upkeep rises for a while. {bot}'s Military strength falls sharply: the scheme ran on its berths.

entries.text: More than half of Military now runs through you, and the Bureau has entered the company as supplier of record. The fleets you supply do not fire. They arrive, they are seen, and the quarrel at the border post ends by itself. The terms are posted and the ledgers can be read, which is dull, and works. Nobody in the Commons sleeps better, because nobody knows how close it was. Harrow Combine still runs its foundries, smaller and watching. The garrisons write you short letters that begin with thanks and end with a requisition.

entries.text: More than half of Luxury moves through you, and the doors are wide. Silk and cut glimmers went where the Plan had never thought to send beauty: the dock mess, the night shift, the school on the ring. Masks that once cost a season's rations were lent at festivals and came back with a stain and a story. Velvet Concord still keeps the grand tables, though fewer people stand at them. The Bureau drafted a form for the allocation of beauty and then, to its credit, left it blank.
entries.place: End screen body, win Luxury, good outcome
End screen heading, win Minerals, good outcome

entries.text: More than half of Minerals comes through you, and most of it went into ground. Ingot from the smelter, alloy from the deep cuts, plate from the fabric: the next ring of homes stands on them, with floors that do not ring when walked. The crews rotate on a posted schedule. Harrow Combine still cuts, at its own pace, in its own corner. The Bureau counted the new homes and found, to its surprise, that a form existed for them. Under the floors the stone is patient. It always was.
entries.place: End screen body, win Minerals, good outcome
End screen heading, win Biotech, good outcome

entries.text: More than half of Biotech passes through you, and it goes out the door. Bio-gel and gene seed reached the terraces at Tillam, the fields at Ashgate and clinics nobody had thought to supply. A cure went out on plain paper, with no licence number, and was copied by hand in rooms the Bureau never saw. Velvet Concord still sells the fine strains to those who can pay. The Plan took the credit, which is its way. In the culture lab the vats hum at the pace of something with all the time it needs.
entries.place: End screen body, win Biotech, good outcome
End screen heading, win Military, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Military runs through you, and the fleets answer. Not to the Commons, and not to you exactly. They answer to the order book, and the order book answers to whoever paid last. The Bureau entered you as supplier of record and asked, very quietly, whether copies of the order forms might reach it first. They cannot. A border post has two flags now and one purchase order. You are never at the front. You only stand where the front is paid for. The racks are full and the cores hum. A great many people are armed, and the Plan has not yet decided what to call it.
entries.place: End screen body, win Military, bad outcome
End screen heading, win Luxury, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Luxury is yours, and everyone wants what only you hold. Prices climb the way stairs do in a dream. Buyers who once haggled now wait, and the ones who cannot wait send guards. Your vaults are lit gold and built like a cell. The Bureau entered you as supplier of record and asked, politely, how many locks. Velvet Concord's masks hang in its empty halls. You hold everything the sky finds beautiful, and no one left may touch it unwatched. The cut glimmers hum faintly as you pass, the way glass does before it breaks.
entries.place: End screen body, win Luxury, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Minerals comes through you, and the seams are paying for it. Cinderrest and Greywake were cut to the bone, and then to the bone beneath. White dust has reached the lamps of more rocks, and the Bureau lists every one as uninhabited. They are not. The crews work each cut to its rim until it is gone. Ingot, alloy and plate leave in long rows, and the dead worlds spread one cut at a time. Harrow Combine's crews drift off to other rock. The glass in the walls hums once, low, where it stopped being a wall.
entries.place: End screen body, win Minerals, bad outcome
End screen heading, win Biotech, bad outcome

entries.text: More than half of Biotech is yours, and the seed is locked. Gene seed leaves the culture lab under a seal and a ticket for every batch. The terraces at Tillam and the fields at Ashgate grow what you allow, on terms the Bureau calls reasonable. Nothing is withheld in anger. It is withheld by paperwork, which is quieter. Velvet Concord cannot sell what your wall will not let it copy. The vats are clean and the shelves are full. In the lab, something small and patented turns toward the light.

entries.text: The company has no ships left, and the cash is still below zero. Each cycle the Bureau took the newest hull to cover the debt, and now the last is gone. Your ships are entered in the Common Ledger, and your name is given a quota that is equal and exactly the size of everyone else's. A clerk reads the closing form aloud and adds that nothing here was ever owed to you. The three rivals go on selling. The sky did not notice.

entries.text: For three cycles running, your company held less than a tenth of every market, and the Bureau has stopped listing you as a competitor. The strongest of the three rivals fills the shelves where yours stood. Your ships still run, and your orders are still taken, politely, at counters that are no longer yours. Nothing cruel was done. A market is a room, and you were not in it.

entries.text: The window closed with no market held. You did not lose. The company is solvent, the ships run, and the Bureau lists you as a participant, a word with no weight. A spread of small shares does not add up to a market. A single market, held all the way, does. The sky has no opinion. It never needed one.

entries.text: Night-shift engineer Pavo Quill ran Voltara's reactors past the safe-hours rule and nothing blew up, so the rule was declared a typo. Energy at Voltara costs less and pays less. The day shift wants the typo back. The cores hum a note nobody tuned.

A grey blight eats Tillam's terraces. The committee ruled it a rumour, since no form reports it, and asked the blight to file one. Food at Tillam costs more and pays more. A Seed Bank lets planet storage hold clearly more against the next one.

Ashgate's harvest came in heavy, and the Common Ledger counted only half. Food at Ashgate costs less and pays less. The other half sits on the dock, real and uncounted, while a dockhand sells it by the sack from a handcart. What is not on the form is still food, until it rots.

A cheerful official explained that hunger is a slow phase of a smooth future, and handed out a booklet on chewing. Food at Voltara costs more and pays more. The cut was equal for all. The crews note that equal is not full.

Winter came early to Tillam and the heaters never stop. Energy at Tillam costs more and pays more. Frost grows inside the ducts in patterns no one will explain. Old duct-keeper Brindle leaves it a cup of warm oil each night. The cup is empty by morning.

A plan arrived at Ashgate this morning, written in a hurry and stamped twice, and every foundry was relit to meet it. Energy at Ashgate costs more and pays more. An old brakeman asked what the rush was. Nobody answered, and the furnaces glared on.

Tillam's dock crews walked out over a debt they say is owed. The Bureau asked where the debt lives, and the crews named the main gate. The port is closed for a while, and routes touching Tillam are blocked until it reopens. Hardy Strains reopens a closed planet a cycle sooner.

Something turned up in Ashgate's lower docks, and the doctors will only say the port is closed. Routes touching Ashgate are blocked until they say otherwise. The dock cat was seen leaving the building at speed. Nobody here is a witness. Everybody is a suspect.

A fault in Voltara's grid took the port with it, so the planet that lights everyone cannot light its own docks. The port is closed for a while, and routes touching Voltara are blocked. The law says lights on. The emergency says off. A clerk decides, by candle.

A lender's agent, a thin man named Shylo Vane, walked Tillam's market and bought every debt in sight. Sellers settled up and dumped their stock. Energy at Tillam costs less and pays less for now. A debt is real until someone stops believing in the paper.

Ashgate foreman Dov Rennick read the numbers, declared the shift had made enough, and sent the crews home. Energy at Ashgate costs less and pays less. Enough is a figure the Plan does not print. By evening three more foremen had found the word.

A trader named Wex whispered on Voltara's docks that the far beacons had gone dark. They had not. Buyers bought energy hard anyway, and the lie came true. Energy at Voltara costs more and pays more. Price Whisper shows next cycle's prices, rumour or not.

A family with old credits quietly bought every food contract on Ashgate. Their agent, a polite man named Corvale, asked only that nobody ask. Food at Ashgate costs more and pays more. The Commons has no form for that question yet.

Inspector Pell counted Voltara's food stores and found them sufficient, on a form. The market believed the form, so food at Voltara costs less and pays less. The pantries are still bare, now correctly accounted for. The form reads smoothly. That is most of truth.

Tillam declared a festival of founders, and everyone wore a founder's mask. Food at Tillam costs more and pays more. Three committees claim to be the real founders. By midnight nobody can tell, and nobody clears the tables.
A ship leaves Tillam half empty

A ship left Tillam half empty, bound for a rock nobody has charted. Those who stayed sold spare food to pay for staying. Food at Tillam costs less and pays less. A letter came back, from a Tillam that chose otherwise. No one has answered it.

Tillam's silk weavers downed tools over a form that counted their hours twice. Silk at Tillam costs more and pays more. An old weaver says to watch the cricket in the vat, which changes shape when it sees another. Fine Finishing makes a Luxury price rise pay clearly more.

Voltara's crews hold a gala to celebrate a quota met on paper. Silk at Voltara costs more and pays more. Everyone borrows a sleeve and a mask for the night, and by the second hour the crews look alike. Patron's List counts sales here as clearly more Luxury share.

A fire swept Voltara's core foundry and left the casting floor black. Logic cores at Voltara cost more and pay more. A cheerful report calls it a gentle step toward a better line. The ash settled on the walls in rows. Nobody has read them.

Ashgate recalled its farm tractors to be retrained as safe. Logic cores at Ashgate cost more and pay more. The retrained ones panic when two foremen give opposite orders. The old ones were told to keep quiet and keep going, and they do.
A rich seam is logged twice

A survey crew found a rich seam and logged it in two offices, so it is counted twice and sold twice. Ore at Voltara costs less and pays less while the news is fresh. With Smelting, ore orders ignore the size cap, so a cheap week can be a big one.

Voltara's foundry ordered more rock than the Plan had dreamed of. Ore at Voltara costs more and pays more. Every shortcut the founders took lies under the furnace floor, and the furnace wants more. Prospecting lets routes start at asteroid clusters, where the rock is free.

The wreck of a hundred ships has settled into orbit over {planet}, and a salvage broker, Captain Rusk, offers to sweep it for a fee. The Bureau filed the wreck as unowned, which is why it is still up there. Routes from {planet} carry less while it stays.
Pay the fee. The debris is cleared and routes from {planet} run as before.
Routes from {planet} carry less while the debris stays. It does not clear itself.

Rusk's tugs swept the orbit and filed the receipt. Routes from {planet} carry their full load again. The wreck went somewhere. The receipt does not say where, and you stopped asking when Rusk started smiling.
You left the wreck. Ships from {planet} thread around it and carry less. The offer stays open. Rusk's tug waits at the edge of the field, as patient as a bill.

Chief engineer Ilya Sorn wants to put a shield across part of the sun. Residents hate it and say so in writing, at length. It would reshape the markets on planets you can buy later: some goods get cheaper, while profit and energy rise. What you already own stays as it is.
Planets you can buy later change: some resources drop, profit and energy rise.
Nothing changes. The sun keeps its full light.

The shield is up and the sky is dimmer. Residents are furious and filed it in triplicate, in the dark. On planets you can buy later, some goods get cheaper while profit and energy climb. Planets you own are untouched. Sorn calls it a clause. The sun calls nothing.
The plans go back in a drawer. Residents are relieved and file no thanks. Nothing changes in any market. Sorn asked what the rush was, and no one had an answer.

Nomad families live on the asteroids you could mine. They are not on the Common Ledger, which the Bureau takes as a personal failing. They count their people by who shares the meal. Evict them and the rock is yours. Or let them stay, and let their lamps burn.
The asteroids open for mining. Some nomads turn to piracy, and pirates rise.
The asteroids stay closed to mining. No pirates come of it.
The nomads left on the next tide, without a word. The rock is yours to mine. Some did not go far, and now they keep ships and a grudge. Pirates rise. The empty tables were left set.
You let the nomads stay. Their lamps burn on the rock, small and steady, and they share a meal with the first ship that docks. The asteroids remain closed to mining.

Pirates now work the lanes, and fewer cargoes get through. Trade volume falls while they stay. The Bureau has opened a file on them. It is a thin file, and so is the fleet behind it. Obedience is cheaper than love, and lasts as long.
Pay to have the pirates cleared. It costs credits and removes their effect on trade.

A rock is coming in on a slow path, and the Bureau noticed it the way it notices everything: late. The state can turn it aside for a fee, and wants it known that it does so out of love. Refusing is a shorter form. Cask Cellar keeps Luxury stock safe from such a cut.
Cost: payment to the state. Asteroid dealt with. The company gains one expansion point.
An even chance: company storage is hit, or nothing happens.

The state turned the rock aside and sent a receipt. The company gains one expansion point for the trouble. The asteroid drifts on, toward someone else's sky. A law is only as strong as the one who says: this is the law.
Event reward: the asteroid is dealt with and the company gains an expansion point.

The asteroid struck {planet}. Your company storage there is gone, and what it held with it. The Bureau has recorded the loss as an adjustment of the Common Ledger. Nobody said sorry. Death takes what a life would still have held.

The asteroid grazed {planet}. Your company storage there is cracked and holds less than before. The Bureau has recorded the damage as "partial". The crack runs through the wall in a straight, patient line.

The asteroid passed the system and kept going. Nothing was hit and nothing changes. The Bureau withdrew its warning, with regret, and kept the form. You could have been struck right now. Let that decide how you read the next notice.

Tillam keeps a reserve of grain behind a lock that only the committee can open. Winter is close and the stores outside are thin. The committee will open it for a company that carries the grain out, and wants an answer today. The lock is old and patient.
Food at Tillam costs less and pays less for a while. Tillam remembers.
Food at Tillam costs more and pays more for a while. Tillam remembers.
Food at Ashgate costs less and pays less for a while. Ashgate remembers.
The lock gave way and the grain went out by hand, sack to sack. Food at Tillam costs less and pays less while the stores are full. The committee recorded it as a loan. Nobody asked who owes whom.

You declined. The lock stayed on and the queue grew in the cold. Food at Tillam costs more and pays more while it is scarce. Somewhere inside the granary something shifted, as if it also had been waiting.

The grain left Tillam by night, on ships that did not ask to be loaded. Food at Ashgate costs less and pays less for a while. The committee at Tillam noticed the empty shelf and wrote a short, cold note.

Tillam remembered the grain. Every heater on the terraces runs high and the committee calls it a gift. Energy at Tillam costs more and pays more for a while. The frost in the ducts has gone quiet, as if it was fed.
The queue that waited in the cold came to the docks. Tillam's port is closed for a while, and routes touching Tillam are blocked. The crowd does not shout. It stands in rows and looks at the ships.

Ashgate remembered the grain. Its foundries run hot in thanks and the smoke leans toward your ships. Energy at Ashgate costs more and pays more for a while. A foreman left a loaf at the dock. It was still warm.

A beacon pulses over Dunmere Reach, from a rock that no chart lists. Its pattern repeats, then changes, as if it had heard the dock talk. The Bureau office at Quillon wants it logged and silenced. The crews want to answer. Your ships pass it every cycle.
Silk at Quillon costs more and pays more for a while. Something answers back.
Quillon closes its port to check the sky. Routes touching Quillon are blocked for a while.

A crew sent three pulses back. The beacon went dark, then lit again, in the same order. Quillon's buyers heard and bought silk as if a festival had been announced. Silk there costs more and pays more. Nobody has said what the festival is for.

The Bureau filed the beacon as a fault and closed Quillon's port to inspect the sky. Routes touching Quillon are blocked for a while. The inspectors were polite. The beacon pulsed once, as if it had read the form.

Small ships came in from the quiet rock and docked at Mossfell without papers. They want food and pay in odd, heavy coins. Food at Mossfell costs more and pays more for a while. They did not say their names. They stayed polite and counted the crates twice.

The inspectors found no fault and Quillon's port reopened. Stock held back for the check came out all at once. Silk at Quillon costs less and pays less for a while. The beacon is still up there. The report says it is not.

The family that bought Ashgate's food contracts sends a polite note. For a share, they will keep the docks quiet and the other traders out. They also mention how fragile a dock can be. The Bureau has no form for this. It would like one.
Food at Ashgate costs more and pays more for a while. The family will call in the favour.
Food at Ashgate costs less and pays less for a while. The family will wait.
Ashgate closes its port for an audit. Routes touching Ashgate are blocked for a while.
The family's people took the docks in the morning, in clean coats. Food at Ashgate costs more and pays more, since their prices travel with them. Everything is quiet. A dock this quiet has an owner.
You sent back a polite no. The family sent back a polite nod. Food at Ashgate costs less and pays less as their buyers step back to watch. Nobody was threatened. Everyone knows what was not said.
The Bureau thanked you in writing and closed Ashgate's port for an audit. Routes touching Ashgate are blocked for a while. The audit will take its own time. The family has been told who filed.

The family closed Ashgate's docks to every ship but its own, and sent you the bill for the quiet. Routes touching Ashgate are blocked for a while. The note was courteous. A favour is a debt that keeps its place.

The family did nothing, which was its answer. Its buyers stayed away from the furnaces and energy at Ashgate costs less and pays less for a while. A courier sits in a booth on the dock, reading and never turning a page.
The audit ends, parts are short

The audit ended and Ashgate's port is open. The family's contracts were frozen and the repair shops cannot get spares. Logic cores at Ashgate cost more and pay more for a while. The Bureau stamped the file closed. The family kept its copy.
Rivet guns pile up at Voltara

Voltara's foundry kept casting rivet guns after the Admiralty's order was filled, since its last line reads until victory. Stacks reach the roof. Rivet guns at Voltara cost less and pay less. A clerk asked if victory knew. Contract Doctrine softens Military price events.
